correctness.rationale: For k-wise independent Bernoulli rows, exact factorial moments are (n)_j(\(\lambda\)/n)^j. Uniform integrability preserves orders below k; lower semicontinuity yields the kth upper bound. The converse constructs nonnegative finite-support laws with exact target moments via a vanishing Poisson mixture and invertible triangular correction; a mass q_n=O(n^-k) at n supplies any positive kth-moment deficit without changing the weak limit. Uniformly random placement of the count gives exchangeable k-wise independent rows.

evidence: The pairwise result fixes the first factorial moment and bounds the second; the three-wise result fixes the first two and bounds the third at unit intensity.
Peled–Yadin–Yehudayoff provide finite-n moment equivalence for k-wise independent counts, but their objective is the extremal probability of all successes.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the pairwise nor the three-wise statement implies the exact classification for every fixed \(k\ge4\) and every \(\lambda\). The finite-n moment equivalence alone does not give the necessary-and-sufficient weak-limit class or show that every admissible limiting law is attainable; that converse is supplied by the explicit truncation, escaping-mass, and triangular-correction construction.

evidence: For exchangeable rows, E(S_n)_j/(n)_j is the probability that any specified j coordinates are all one; inclusion-exclusion recovers every pattern probability.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The falling-factorial formulation is equivalent to the finite-n count-moment formulation. The new statement adds the exact weak-limit constraints and converse for arbitrary fixed \(k\ge4\) and \(\lambda\).

originality.rationale: The new scope is the exact all-order weak-limit classification for fixed \(k\ge4\) and arbitrary fixed \(\lambda\), including attainability. The indexed pairwise and unit-intensity three-wise classifications are lower-order special cases; the inspected primary papers address finite-n moment representations or posterior moments, not this weak-limit class. Residual risk from unindexed or routine generalizations is stated explicitly.
residual_risks: Searches may miss unindexed or differently worded work that classifies weak limits for arbitrary fixed k and \(\lambda\).

The all-order theorem may be viewed as a natural extension of the pairwise and three-wise classifications; the value is the complete hierarchy plus the exact attainability construction, not a claim that the proof technique is unprecedented.
Independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.

value.rationale: This is a complete necessary-and-sufficient classification of a natural family of weak limits for every fixed independence order \(k\ge4\) and intensity \(\\(\lambda\)>0\). It identifies precisely the moment order where weak convergence can lose mass and proves every admissible limit is attainable, rather than giving only a necessary bound or one example.
